learn.title: Floating Solar Farms on Water
learn.intro: Floating solar farms revolutionize energy and water conservation by combining renewable power generation with water body preservation. These systems reduce land use conflicts, minimize evaporation, and enhance efficiency through cooling effects. As India targets 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030, floating solar offers scalable solutions for water-stressed regions while accelerating the clean energy transition.
learn.c1_text: Floating solar avoids competing with agriculture or urban areas, preserving fertile land. In drought-prone areas like Rajasthan, water bodies can host solar arrays without disrupting local ecosystems. Over 300 GW of India's solar potential exists on reservoirs, reducing pressure on scarce arable land while generating clean power.
learn.c2_text: Solar panels act as a partial cover, reducing water loss by 30-50% in reservoirs. This mimics a greenhouse effect, conserving water for irrigation and drinking. For example, a 50 MW floating plant in Kerala's Koyna Dam saves ~100 million liters of water annually, equivalent to 400 Olympic swimming pools.
learn.c3_text: Gujarat's Statue of Unity floating solar project (500 MW) demonstrates India's leadership in this tech. The Konkan Coast aims for 20 GW by 2025, leveraging coastal water bodies. MNRE supports such initiatives through subsidies, aligning with India's 500 GW renewable target and water security goals under the National Water Mission.
learn.stat1: India: 300 GW solar potential on reservoirs (2023)
learn.stat2: Floating solar reduces evaporation by up to 50%
learn.stat3: Konkan Coast targets 20 GW floating solar by 2025
learn.stat4: Kerala's Koyna Dam project saves 100 million liters yearly

learn.title: Agrivoltaics: Solar and Farming Together
learn.intro: Agrivoltaics merges solar panels with agriculture, creating dual-use land systems that boost both energy and food production. This innovative approach addresses land scarcity, enhances crop resilience, and generates additional farmer income. With India's agricultural sector employing 42% of the workforce, agrivoltaics offers a sustainable pathway to meet energy and food demands simultaneously.
learn.c1_text: Solar panels elevated above crops allow sunlight penetration, creating microclimates that reduce water evaporation by 30%. Crops like tomatoes and lettuce thrive under partial shade, while panels generate electricity. A 1 MW agrivoltaic system in Spain increased land productivity by 60%, demonstrating scalable benefits for food-energy nexus solutions.
learn.c2_text: Some crops, like grapes and lettuce, yield 25-30% more under solar panels due to reduced heat stress. The panels' height (2-4 meters) allows machinery access, improving farm efficiency. In Arizona trials, agrivoltaics boosted alfalfa yields by 18% while generating 120 MWh of solar energy daily, proving mutual benefits for farmers and utilities.
learn.c3_text: India's Gujarat Energy Development Agency launched agrivoltaic pilots in Kutch, combining 1 MW solar plants with mustard cultivation. Farmers receive 20% extra income from solar lease payments. The model aligns with MNRE's vision for sustainable land use, supporting India's 500 GW renewable target while enhancing rural livelihoods through dual revenue streams.
learn.stat2: Agrivoltaics can increase land productivity by 60%
learn.stat4: Solar panels reduce crop water needs by 30%

learn.title: Hydrogen Color Code Explained
learn.intro: Understanding hydrogen's color code is crucial for navigating the clean energy transition. Blue, green, and grey hydrogen differ in production methods, environmental impact, and scalability. As India aims for 5 million tons of hydrogen by 2030, distinguishing these types helps policymakers and investors prioritize sustainable options aligned with net-zero goals.
learn.c1_text: Grey hydrogen is produced via steam methane reforming (SMR), emitting 9-12 tons of CO2 per ton of hydrogen. It's cheap (~$1.50/kg) but unsustainable. Over 95% of global hydrogen is grey, making it the default today. In India, Reliance's Jamnagar plant produces grey hydrogen for fertilizer production, highlighting its industrial role despite high emissions.
learn.c2_text: Blue hydrogen uses SMR but captures 60-90% of CO2 via CCS. Costs rise to $2-3/kg due to capture technology. While better than grey, it requires infrastructure for CO2 storage. Shell's Quest project in Canada captures 90% of emissions, proving viability. However, methane leakage during extraction remains a challenge for climate benefits.
learn.c3_text: Green hydrogen uses electrolysis powered by renewables, emitting zero direct CO2. Costs are higher ($3-6/kg) but falling rapidly. India's Green Hydrogen Mission aims for 5 MMT capacity by 2030, with NTPC's 10 MW plant in Gujarat. The IEA notes green hydrogen could supply 20% of global energy by 2050, vital for hard-to-abate sectors like steel and shipping.

learn.stat2: Green hydrogen costs drop to $2/kg by 2030 (IEA)
learn.stat3: Grey hydrogen emits 12 tons CO2 per ton produced
learn.stat4: Global hydrogen market to reach $300 billion by 2030

learn.title: India's Renewable Purchase Obligation
learn.intro: India's Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) mandates distribution utilities to source a percentage of power from renewables, driving the country's clean energy transition. DISCOMs must comply annually, with penalties for non-compliance. This policy underpins India's 500 GW renewable target by 2030, ensuring grid stability and private sector investment in solar and wind projects across states.
learn.c1_text: DISCOMs must purchase 25.5% renewable energy by 2025, rising to 40% by 2030. Non-compliance attracts penalties up to Rs 1,000/kW shortfall. States like Tamil Nadu lead with 35% compliance, while others struggle with financial constraints. The RPO ensures steady demand for renewables, attracting investments like Adani's 20 GW solar portfolio.
learn.c2_text: Each state has tailored RPO targets based on renewable potential. For example, Rajasthan (30.5%) and Gujarat (27.5%) have high targets due to abundant solar/wind resources. Haryana's 20% target includes 10% for rooftop solar. MNRE monitors progress via quarterly reports, adjusting targets through amendments to maintain national momentum toward 500 GW.
learn.c3_text: Tamil Nadu achieved 35% RPO compliance in 2023, exceeding its 30% target. The state leveraged 15 GW solar and 7 GW wind capacity, supported by strong policy frameworks. TNEB Ltd's renewable purchases rose 40% YoY, demonstrating how RPO drives DISCOM modernization. The model inspires other states to adopt similar strategies for energy security and climate commitments.

learn.stat3: Tamil Nadu achieved 35% RPO compliance in 2023

learn.title: Direct Air Carbon Capture Technology
learn.intro: Direct Air Carbon Capture (DAC) removes CO2 directly from ambient air, offering a scalable solution for negative emissions. Powered by renewables, DAC complements India's net-zero 2070 pledge by offsetting hard-to-abate sectors. With atmospheric CO2 at 420 ppm, DAC technology is critical for achieving climate goals while supporting green hydrogen and synthetic fuel production through carbon recycling.
learn.c1_text: DAC uses chemical sorbents to capture CO2 from 1,000 cubic meters of air, yielding 0.5 kg of CO2 per kg of sorbent. Climeworks' Orca plant in Iceland captures 4,000 tons/year using geothermal energy. In India, renewable-powered DAC units could utilize excess solar power, making it viable for rural areas with high solar potential and industrial emission zones.
learn.c2_text: DAC requires 3-6 MWh of electricity per ton of CO2 captured. Solar/wind power reduces costs to $150-200/ton, down from $600/ton in 2020. India's 500 GW renewable target by 2030 could supply DAC plants with affordable clean energy. The IEA notes DAC needs 1% of global renewable capacity by 2050, aligning with India's green hydrogen ambitions.
learn.c3_text: India's National Carbon Offset Policy allows DAC for compliance under its 2070 net-zero goal. The government supports DAC R&D through DST and MNRE grants. Projects like Tata Chemicals' DAC pilot in Gujarat aim to capture 10,000 tons/year by 2025. DAC integration with green hydrogen plants could create circular carbon economies, supporting India's climate leadership in emerging economies.
learn.stat2: DAC costs drop to $150/ton with renewable energy
learn.stat3: Global DAC capacity to reach 500 Mt/year by 2030 (IEA)
learn.stat4: India's net-zero target by 2070 requires DAC scale-up

learn.title: Solid-State Battery Revolution
learn.intro: Solid-state batteries promise safer, denser energy storage by replacing liquid electrolytes with solid materials. This breakthrough addresses safety risks of lithium-ion batteries, enabling longer EV ranges and faster charging. As India pushes for 30% EV adoption by 2030, solid-state batteries could transform transportation and grid storage, supporting its 500 GW renewable target with efficient energy management.
learn.c1_text: Solid electrolytes eliminate fire/explosion risks from liquid leakage, while offering 2-3x higher energy density (500 Wh/kg vs 250 Wh/kg). Toyota's prototype achieves 1,200 Wh/kg, enabling 1,000 km EV ranges. The US DOE highlights their potential for aerospace and grid storage, where safety and longevity are critical for renewable integration and transportation sectors.
learn.c2_text: Solid-state batteries operate at higher voltages (up to 5V) and temperatures, with faster charging (10-15 minutes to 80%). They use lithium metal anodes, doubling cycle life to 10,000 cycles. Samsung's 2023 prototype demonstrated 1,000 km range with 10-minute charging. These features make them ideal for India's EV ambitions, including 300 million vehicles by 2040.
learn.c3_text: India's National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems funds solid-state R&D. Tata Chemicals and Ather Energy collaborate on indigenous batteries for two-wheelers. The PLI scheme offers $2.6 billion incentives for 50 GWh battery manufacturing by 2030. Solid-state adoption could reduce import dependence on China, which supplies 70% of India's EV batteries, boosting energy security and job creation.
learn.stat2: Solid-state batteries offer 500 Wh/kg energy density
